units.title: Measures of economic performance
points: Distinguish GDP, GNI and GDP per capita as measures of living standards
Calculate and interpret real vs nominal GDP and the GDP deflator
Explain limitations of GDP as a measure of welfare and well-being
Define inflation and calculate CPI inflation from an index
Distinguish unemployment and underemployment; define balance of payments

units.title: Aggregate demand and aggregate supply
points: Draw and shift AD; identify the components C+I+G+(X−M)
Explain SRAS and LRAS shifts, including Keynesian LRAS shape
Show equilibrium changes and analyse multiplier effects
Distinguish demand-pull and cost-push inflation on the AD/AS diagram

units.title: National income and the multiplier
points: Explain the circular flow of income and injections/withdrawals
Calculate the multiplier from MPC/MPM and apply it to a change in AD
Distinguish nominal and real values in national income data

units.title: Causes of economic growth
points: Distinguish actual from potential growth; use PPF and LRAS
Explain growth from investment, productivity, technology and education
Evaluate the costs and benefits of growth for different stakeholders
Assess whether growth is sustainable and inclusive

units.title: Causes and effects of inflation
points: Explain demand-pull, cost-push and imported inflation
Analyse effects of inflation on consumers, firms, savers and exporters
Explain deflation, disinflation and risks of a deflationary spiral
Evaluate the costs of inflation against those of deflation

units.title: Causes and effects of unemployment
points: Distinguish frictional, structural, cyclical and seasonal unemployment
Explain the natural rate and real-wage unemployment on a diagram
Analyse effects on workers, firms, government and the economy
Evaluate whether unemployment always involves welfare loss

units.title: Balance of payments and exchange rates
points: Explain the current and financial accounts and their components
Relate current account deficit to capital/financial account surplus
Explain floating, fixed and managed exchange rate systems
Analyse causes and consequences of a current account deficit
Evaluate the effect of depreciation/appreciation on J-curve and exports

units.title: Policies to achieve objectives
points: Classify fiscal, monetary and supply-side policy instruments
Explain transmission mechanisms from policy to objectives
Analyse policy conflicts, e.g. inflation vs unemployment, growth vs deficit
Evaluate effectiveness using time lags, expectations and crowding out

units.title: Globalisation and international trade
points: Explain causes of globalisation: trade, technology, MNCs
Analyse benefits and drawbacks of trade and specialisation
Explain protectionism: tariffs, quotas, subsidy; effects on stakeholders
Evaluate arguments for and against protectionism

units.title: Trading blocs, WTO and global inequality
points: Distinguish free trade areas, customs unions and single markets
Analyse trade creation and trade diversion
Assess the role of the WTO and the limits of its influence
Explain causes of national and global inequality and policies to reduce it

units.title: Emerging and developing economies
points: Explain growth strategies and factors driving emerging economies
Analyse effects of growth on living standards and the environment
Assess effects of MNCs and aid on developing economies
Evaluate why growth strategies differ in their outcomes

units.title: Exam technique and data response
points: Interpret and use data, index numbers and percentage changes
Structure 5, 8, 10, 12 and 25 mark answers with analysis and evaluation
Apply a chain of reasoning: point, diagram, mechanism, effect
Use evidence from the stimulus extract and an analytical framework to judge
Plan 25-mark essays with two or three developed arguments each side
